questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Iceland because of it's amazing nature, which I would not see anywhere else.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, and the international division was always very helpful and quick to answer questions on email and by phonecall.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I participated in a welcome-event with all the other exchange students. It consisted of 3 days with different events to inform us on both academic and personal stuff about what it is like to move to a new country.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We could chose a room with shared kitchen (which I chose) and an apartment for yourself, which was more expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a shared kitchen with 9 other people. Unfortunately it was not very nice, because the cleaning condition was horrible and people were really bad at cleaning.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: In my experience it was not a very social place, which I was very disappointed about. The people who lived at 'Gamli' had it so much better both with the facilities and the social aspect. So choose that one if you can! Also the room is not very cozy, you have to buy your own furniture except for bed, table and chair.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You got the courses you applied for in the application for exchange, and if you wanted to change them when you arrived, you just had to fill out what courses you are taking on the student page. It was very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international division was always there to help you by email, or in their office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I wanted, you just have to make sure yourself, that the timetables fit with each other, so none of them overlap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
As soon as you know you are going to University of Iceland, apply for student housing, because the waitlist is very long. 
Remember to check the course page on how exams are and the class timetables, so you know they fit you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could only take masters-courses for my home university, which was unfortunate because most of the BA-courses were a lot more interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much more like highschool teaching. They took attendance in one of my classes, there was a lot of group work and presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Second Language theories and pedagogy.
Theory and writing.
Cultural studies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think cultural studies was very interesting but it was just not very organised.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to rent my room two months before I was arriving, so two months of rent = 12000 kr.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, vegetables was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a gym, which was very cheap and nice, where you could also take som classes for yoga. You could also participate in the school choir.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the yoga-classes were nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car on the weekends and go for a trip around Iceland with your fellow students!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, not much different from DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get in the WhatsApp group with all the other exchange students, and go with people on trips from here.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Icelanders are not very open. The three icelanders who lived in my kitchen did not want to talk at all.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their relationship with the nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find housing early or apply for student housing early.
Remember warm clothes. 
Always just go with the opportunities of trips around iceland, even though it is with new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It is normal to feel lost, or like you don't belong, and homesick. Many other people feel the same way.
You can always ask your teachers for help with anything, they are very helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the icelandic nature I got to see. So many beautiful places, and I definitely recommend going around the ringroad of the whole island, which you can do in a week.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I didn't feel I got to know people good enough, so I felt alone a lot of the time, and missing home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
